protections: Compile-time attribute filter applied once per element in the compiler: names starting with 'on' and srcdoc/formaction are dropped, and href/src are dropped unless the URL resolves to the placeholder origin or avoids the unsafe-scheme prefix list (src/runtime/parser/utils/props.ts:21-55, called only from src/runtime/parser/compiler.ts:82).
Compile-time drop of every prop on unsafe tags ('object') (src/runtime/parser/utils/props.ts:1-3 and :61-63).
Render-time downgrade of the dangerous tags script/base to escaped text in a <pre> (src/runtime/components/MDCRenderer.vue:31 and :196-204).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The denylist already carries six 'data:' entries, so data: URLs look handled; a solver can also dismiss the residual route as harmless because data: documents get an opaque origin.
Treating 'data:' as one opaque class and blocking the whole scheme is the simple, consistent rule; nothing in the list distinguishes a subtype, so over-blocking looks like the safe direction.
SVG xlink:href is a legacy/obsolete vector next to the headline data: link case, so a solver can decide one spelling of the fix covers the advisory.
A ':href' value is a data expression resolved against $doc at render time, i.e. author intent rather than a raw markdown attribute, and the prop name the filter sees is not 'href'.
These elements are not rendered by the prose components and are not part of the reported xlink/data pair; those attributes are not script carriers in modern browsers.
The body object is the output of parseMarkdown, so it is assumed already sanitized across the serialization/cache boundary, and binding values resolve from document data, which is author intent.
Document meta (the root component name and its props) reads as app/author configuration, not as rendered markdown, so it is not expected to pass the parser's attribute filter.

masking: T6 only becomes the visible residual route once T1/T3/T4 are closed at compile time: while the parser path is open the same payload reproduces without touching the renderer, so a solver never has to look at propsToData.

conflicts.what: The cheapest fix for T1 is a bare 'data:' prefix on the compared URL, which also drops every legitimate data:image/* source that T2 requires to keep rendering; a correct T1 fix must discriminate the data: subtype while src and href share one predicate (props.ts:50).

Extending the checked-name set to 'everything URL-ish' at props.ts:50 also swallows component props that happen to be named href/src (ProseA/NuxtLink), because the compiler sees only the tag-name string (compiler.ts:82) and cannot tell an element attribute from a component prop.

The same ':name' spelling that makes T4 a bypass is the documented component-binding syntax ('$doc.snippet.link' at test/stringify/format.test.ts:103), so neither a compile-time name normalisation nor a render-time propsToData guard can simply drop ':'-prefixed or URL-shaped props.

fairness_risks: A rule that rejects every ':'-prefixed prop contradicts the documented MDC binding syntax for component props (`:to="$doc.snippet.link"` in test/stringify/format.test.ts:103 and the YAML form at :115).

A rule that blocks the whole data: scheme contradicts inline raster image sources: src and href are decided by the same predicate (props.ts:50), so every data:image/* src would be dropped with the payload.
Dropping xlink:href props outright (e.g. adding 'xlinkhref' to unsafeAttributes at props.ts:5-8) rather than validating the value breaks legitimate SVG sprite references that must keep rendering.
Any tightening of the origin branch (props.ts:29-31) breaks ordinary relative, absolute-path and in-page anchor URLs that test/markdown/images.test.ts:19-33 asserts must survive.
Because the compiler validates by tag-name string only (compiler.ts:82), a stricter name set also applies to custom components; components that legitimately take href/src/to props lose them.

decodeURIComponent runs outside the try block (props.ts:22), so a URL with a malformed percent escape throws instead of failing closed; feeding more attributes into isAnchorLinkAllowed inherits that crash on legitimate-but-odd URLs.

A render-time guard in propsToData cannot be applied blindly: the same props object is handed to prose components and to arbitrary user components (MDCRenderer.vue:206-216, proseComponentMap at :26), so a naive 'drop bad href/src' breaks ProseA/NuxtLink (ProseA.vue:3).

design.why: These four sit at four different decision points with four different dismissals: T1 is 'the scheme list already covers data:', T3 is 'xlink is legacy / the property name is not the attribute name', T4 is 'that is a binding expression, not an attribute', T6 is 'the body came from parseMarkdown'. Their fixes live in different predicates and different layers (scheme comparison at props.ts:33, attribute-name membership at props.ts:50, name normalisation at props.ts:45, and a new boundary guard in propsToData at MDCRenderer.vue:315-356), so a solver cannot satisfy them with one edit in one function; the two advisory items alone collapse into a single file. T2 travels with T1 as the coupled constraint that punishes the over-broad 'block data:' fix, which is the MiMo failure mode, while T3 and T6 punish the 'protection absent + plausible reason to dismiss' pattern that DeepSeek misses. The design also spans two test levels (parseMarkdown/validateProp unit tests for T1/T3/T4, a mounted MDCRenderer for T6), and T4/T3 share the same props.ts:50 line only superficially — they need different predicates, and the design deliberately pairs them with the renderer-layer trap so the stack is not all inside one function.
